title: Damp-Heat Stability of MAPbI3 Perovskite Solar Cells

paragraphs.text: We examine the operational stability of MAPbI3 perovskite solar cells under damp-heat stress at 85 C and 85% relative humidity.
MAPbI3 films were prepared following a two-step sequential deposition method inside a nitrogen glovebox.
The devices use a mesoporous TiO2 scaffold deposited from a commercial Dyesol 18NR-T paste by screen printing.
After 500 h of damp-heat aging, the champion device retained a PCE of 18.7%, down from an initial value of 20.3%.
The hysteresis index of fresh devices was measured as 0.04 before aging.
The ISOS-D-2 protocol was followed for all damp-heat tests.
UV-Vis spectra indicate an optical band gap of 1.57 eV for the MAPbI3 films.
Impedance spectroscopy revealed a strong increase in recombination after aging.
Devices were tested without encapsulation during damp-heat exposure.
MAPbI3 here refers to the same compound methylammonium lead iodide studied in earlier ambient-fabrication work.
TiO2 paste batch 18NR-T lot 42 was used for all devices in this study.
Stability data for all devices are available in the repository.
